document_title: Alaska Bought American. The Tariff Found a Seam.
post_copy:
"Search and rescue" appears once in Proclamation 11055, at the end of a list of federal drone uses. The document never says Alaska.

Ryan Marlow of Alaska DOT and PF calls the technology "crucial aerial support for search and rescue". Alaska's $12.4 million SOAR initiative funds drones and docking stations for rural Alaska.

The duty is charged at the border. Phase one flew Skydio X10s. Skydio says the X10 is assembled in the U.S. A maker's statement is not a customs ruling. The 25 percent components duty lands February 9th, 2027.

The four duty bands as the proclamation words them, both effective dates, zero mentions of Alaska, and two blanks in Alaska's fleet record.

On paper, thermal imagers get their own 100 percent band with no weight limit. The X10 weighs 2.1 kilograms and takes a thermal camera. Which band does the tariff line put it in?

#Section232 #DroneTariffs #RuralAlaska

slides.headline: Alaska bought American. The tariff found another door.
The duty is charged at the border, not at the factory.
slides.body: Proclamation 11055 sets 100 percent on imported drones over 25 kilograms, on imported drones with thermal imagers, and on imported docking stations. It attaches to goods entered for consumption from 12:01 a.m. eastern, September 3rd.
slides.body_second: Alaska's grant bought drones, docking stations and Starlink for communities off the road system.

slides.headline: What the border charges, by shape.
slides.scope_flag: ANNEX I SETS THE ACTUAL SCOPE BY TARIFF LINE. THIS DECK DOES NOT QUOTE IT.
slides.footnote: 25 kilograms sits within a hair of the FAA's 55 pound small aircraft ceiling. The two lines coincide.

slides.headline: August 11th to 13th, on Baranof Island.
slides.body: A thermal drone team joined the search near Port Armstrong for a missing hiker, per KCAW. The proclamation was signed on the 13th.

slides.headline: The word Alaska is not in it.
slides.body: The proclamation names search and rescue once, in a list of what federal agencies use drones for. Alaska, rural, public safety and firefighting don't appear at all. Alaska DOT and PF's Ryan Marlow calls the technology "crucial aerial support for search and rescue".

slides.headline: The seam is inside the airframe.
slides.body: Skydio says the X10 is designed, assembled and supported in the U.S. through "trusted manufacturing partners". That is a maker's statement, not a customs ruling. A second tranche puts 25 percent on imported components from February 9th, 2027.
slides.card_gimbal: THERMAL PAYLOAD, LISTED AT 640 x 512 PX / C34

slides.headline: Two things about this box aren't public.
slides.body: No source says where the docking station is assembled. No public number says how many imported drones Alaska agencies fly. The grant bought drones, docking stations and Starlink for communities off the road system.

slides.headline: Four rates, two effective dates.

slides.mono_note: THE DELAY CLAUSE READS 180 DAYS FROM THE DATE OF THE PROCLAMATION. IT PRINTS NO DATE. 180 DAYS AFTER AUGUST 13, 2026 IS FEBRUARY 9, 2027, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC.

aftercare: Post Tuesday through Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time. August 20th, 2026 is a Thursday, so this draft can go up inside today's window, and holding it to next Tuesday costs nothing but freshness on a proclamation published August 19th, 2026.

Paste the first comment source block within 60 seconds of posting, before the first reader lands. The close slide promises sources in comments and an empty comment field breaks that promise in public.
Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. That window is where reach is decided, and this topic will draw operators and procurement people who expect an answer.

Expect the classification question back. Answer with what the text says, that thermal imagers are listed as their own 100 percent category with no weight condition, and that Annex I sets the actual scope by tariff line. Do not offer a customs opinion.

If someone asks whether Skydio is on the Blue UAS Cleared List, say the list was not reachable during the run and the deck deliberately does not rely on it. Do not confirm or deny listing from memory.
If anyone connects the Baranof search to the state program, correct it. The KCAW report names neither the operator nor the aircraft, and the deck draws no line between them.
At 48 hours, note saves, comments and the save to impression ratio, and log whether the classification question or the components date drew the most replies.
editor_notes_for_email:
SCORE 8.39, ships. Four revision rounds: 7.62, then 7.99, then a round three that produced 8.39 on the criteria and was capped to 6.9 by one text overlap, then 8.39 clean. The round four threshold on the ladder is 7.7, but the deck also clears the unrelaxed 8.3, so nothing here was banked on the relaxation. Machine QA finished at PASS with zero fails AND zero warns on all nine slides, the first clean pass of the run, and all sixteen gate rows are green.

WHAT THIS RUN WAS ACTUALLY ABOUT. The first pixel critic round returned a mean of 4.28 out of 10 while every machine gate read green. The gates check that a declaration exists and is internally consistent; they can't check that it landed on the thing it names. Found that way and fixed: slide 06's dashed origin contours, the deck's central accuracy device, were hardcoded screen ellipses while the parts they name were projected from a 3D camera, so every one enclosed bare foam; slide 09's declared inspection window sat under its own snow cap; contact shadows on 05 and 09 were composited after their objects and painted across their faces, so a solid read as glass; slide 08's rate bars stood on a rail whose x is a declared date axis; and slide 02 published a citation attributing 91 FR 53699 to a claim that doesn't cover it.

SITE SIGN-OFF: PASS, 81 pages, 18 checks. GAS WATCH: PASS, read 2026-08-19, 15 days on record, no gaps, chart present, and the model misses observed EIA deliveries by 6.82 percent. SITE FIXES this run: the sticky nav scrim was raised from .78 to .92 with an opaque @supports fallback, because .78 is a glass value that only works when the blur actually composites and it doesn't everywhere.

MACHINE UPGRADES this run, all three verified by running the thing they changed. First, an art helper now refuses an option it doesn't know: AK.reliefShade validates its option list and throws, and qa.py promotes that to a hard fail. This existed because two slides passed an option called mix that reliefShade has never had, so what was authored as a 30 percent finish was a 100 percent overwrite, and slide 05's cold white bond printed as kraft with every printed line on both sheets erased, leaving the gold marker highlighting a blank sheet. Second, a new plan drift gate cross-checks the storyboard's claims index and each dossier's declared counts against the build. Third, screen-space annotation can now be derived from the camera with AKT.screenBox instead of typed.

THE NEW GATES IMMEDIATELY FOUND DEFECTS IN THIS DECK, after it had merged. Three more reliefShade options that were never applied, an encoding declaration on slide 05 that stopped holding when the gold marker was realigned, and seven plan versus build drifts in the storyboard. All are fixed with zero pixel change and recorded in runs/2026-08-20/CORRECTIONS.md. The shipped storyboard.md was left untouched and the reconciled copy added beside it as storyboard.corrected.md, because overwriting a shipped run artifact is one of the three things this project stops and asks about.

KNOWN SHORTFALLS, read these before posting. Slide 06 is the weakest frame and the named one: its exploded assembly doesn't read as an airframe at any size, so the deck's crux is carried by the caption rather than the art. At 432px slide 07's dashed PLANNED rows collapse into noise, so the 22 versus 35 comparison that slide exists to make doesn't survive the feed test. Slide 07's third sentence repeats slide 02's second body line almost word for word. Slide 01's gold hatch seam is fully contained rather than cut by the right edge, so the cover's edge tease into slide 02 doesn't exist. The caption is 897 characters against a 900 ceiling, so there is no room to add a word at post time.

ACCURACY GUARDRAILS, all held. The proclamation exempts nobody and its duty is triggered by importation. "Skydio says" is the framing on U.S. assembly and never an assertion. No claim is made about which X10 parts are imported, which is why the interior contours are dashed phantom and labelled ORIGIN NOT ESTABLISHED HERE. The components tranche is 25 percent and never 100. SOAR and SMART and ARROW stay three separate names. The 25 kilogram line and the FAA's 55 pound ceiling are said to coincide and never that one adopted the other. The missing hiker on Baranof is not named and is not connected to Alaska DOT and PF, to SOAR or to Skydio. One tense shade worth knowing: the caption's "funds drones and docking stations" reads present tense where Alaska Business Magazine's January 17th, 2025 sentence is future tense, so if a reader pushes, the honest reply is that the article describes what the funding will buy.
